statements.t: Our principal operations target the Utica and Marcellus formations in eastern Ohio and the SCOOP Woodford and Springer formations in central Oklahoma.

To accomplish these goals, we generally allocate capital to projects we believe offer the highest rate of return and we deploy leading drilling and completion techniques and technologies in our development efforts.
We spud 5 gross (4.8 net) wells targeting the Utica and Marcellus formations during the three months ended September 30, 2026.

We strive to maintain sufficient liquidity to ensure financial flexibility, withstand commodity price volatility, fund our development projects, operations and capital expenditures and return capital to shareholders.
There is no guarantee that the debt or equity capital markets will be available to us on acceptable terms or at all.
Our natural gas, oil and NGL derivative activities, when combined with our sales of natural gas, oil and NGL, allow us to predict with greater certainty the total revenue we will receive.
Our capital investment strategy is focused on prudently developing our existing properties to generate sustainable cash flow considering current and forecasted commodity prices.

Also, we currently expect to spend approximately $35.0 million in 2026 for maintenance land and seismic investments, primarily focused on near-term drilling programs and facilitating increases in our working interests and lateral footage in units we plan to drill in 2026, 2027 and 2028.
We expect this capital program to result in approximately 1.030 to 1.055 Bcfe per day of production in 2026.

During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, we spud 21 gross (20.4 net) operated wells and commenced sales from 20 gross (19.7 net) operated wells targeting the Utica and Marcellus for a total incurred cost of approximately $330.5 million.
Our natural gas, oil and NGL derivative activities, when combined with our sales of natural gas, oil and NGL, allow us to predict with greater certainty the revenue we will receive.
We do not enter into derivative contracts for volumes in excess of our share of forecasted production.

We review our derivative positions continuously and if future market conditions change and prices are at levels we believe could jeopardize the effectiveness of a position, we intend to mitigate this risk by either negotiating a cash settlement with our counterparty, restructuring the position or entering a new trade that effectively reverses the current position.
Our hedge arrangements may expose us to risk of financial loss in certain circumstances, including instances where production is less than expected or commodity prices increase.

The disclosure controls and procedures are also intended to ensure that such information is accumulated and communicated to management, including our CEO, in his capacities as our principal executive officer and interim principal financial officer, as appropriate to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosures.

In designing and evaluating the Company's disclosure controls and procedures, management recognizes that any controls and procedures, no matter how well designed and operated, can provide only reasonable, and not absolute, assurance that the objectives of the control system will be met.

statements.t: We expect to continue building on that strength in the fourth quarter, keeping us on track to deliver full-year production and capital expenditures in line with our guidance.”

Dell’Osso continued, “We also continued to enhance the depth of our inventory, completing the Ohio state land acquisitions, and expect to complete our $140 million 2026 discretionary acreage acquisition program by year-end through disciplined, targeted leasing in the core of our position.

As we look to 2027, we are evaluating a more continuous two-rig Appalachia development program, which we believe will drive meaningful operational efficiencies through steadier rig and crew utilization, lower our development costs, concentrate capital in our highest-return asset area and position the business for production growth beginning in 2028.

This shift in capital allocation would allow Gulfport to balance reinvestment with returns to shareholders while preserving our strong balance sheet, and we look forward to sharing our full 2027 outlook in February.”
Both agreements will be supplied using the Company’s existing firm transportation capacity and are priced off sales indices positioned to benefit from growing regional power demand.
Gulfport enters into commodity derivative contracts on a portion of its expected future production volumes to mitigate the Company’s exposure to commodity price fluctuations.
Our principal properties are located in eastern Ohio targeting the Utica and Marcellus formations and in central Oklahoma targeting the SCOOP Woodford and Springer formations.
